sources.title: Erich Kettenhofen, Dvin ,  Encyclopaedia Iranica (1996)
sources.note: Directly read. Paragraphs on Arab conquest, the caliphal governor until 789, subsequent rule, and twentieth-century excavations. Dvin lies just outside this imported outline; material from the city is regional context.

sources.title: Ghewond, History ,  introduction by translator Robert Bedrosian (2006)
sources.note: Directly read. Late eighth-century Armenian historian; covers approximately 632 to 788. Introduction describes caliphal Arminiya, failed rebellions, Bagratid patronage and thirteenth-century surviving manuscript. Counted with chapter 4 as ONE underlying work.

sources.title: Ghewond, History, chapters 17 to 23 ,  Robert Bedrosian translation
sources.note: Directly read chapters 17 and 21: Hisham census and taxation; Marwan appoints Ashot; cavalry stipend arrears. Political testimony explicitly attributed to the author. Combined budget with the introduction.

sources.title: Hakob Papazian, Armenia VI: Armeno-Iranian relations in the Islamic period ,  Encyclopaedia Iranica (1986)
sources.note: Directly read the Umayyad and Abbasid legal-status paragraphs. Uses only community status and jizya; does not reproduce the article’s polemical generalizations.

sources.title: A. A. Kalantaryan, Material culture of Dvin, fifth to eighth centuries (1970)
sources.note: Original institutional PDF indexed English summary and plate list checked; direct PDF download encountered a site challenge, not a full visual page inspection. Summary describes vessels, glass and water mains. Plates XXXVIII (saddled toy horse, sixth to seventh centuries), XXXIX (glass, fifth to eighth centuries), XLI (inkpot and inscribed tile, fifth to eighth centuries), and oil-lamp captions. Broad dating is preserved.

sources.title: Zarifa Alikperova, Talin Cathedral ,  Courtauld Crossing Frontiers
sources.note: Full text directly checked, including seven-line Armenian transcription. Water inscription on two adjacent blocks of southwestern pier: Armenian era 232, 15 May 783 to 13 May 784. Sample is the uninterrupted three-word phrase in line 3, with editorial transliteration and literal translation. No claim of personally deciphering a photograph.

sources.title: Tim Greenwood, Ananias of Shirak ,  Encyclopaedia Iranica (2018)
sources.note: Directly read. Seventh-century educational context, autobiography, Tychikos’s Greek and Armenian teaching and library including medical compositions; no claim of a known eighth-century public-school or hospital system.

sources.title: Vahagn Aslanyan, The mathematical work of Anania Shirakatsi (2024)
sources.note: Full relevant sections read: introduction, problems 6, 7, 13 and 14, solutions, entertaining puzzles. Scholar supplies mathematically coherent translations based on Armenian editions; the scenarios are instructional literature, not household census data. Seventh-century work preserved in later copies.

sources.title: Cyril Toumanoff, Kamsarakan ,  Encyclopaedia Iranica (2010)
sources.note: Directly read. Princely territories, northern frontier position and sale of principalities after failed anti-Arab rebellion. Its 771 to 772 dating differs from modern dating of the major 774 to 775 revolt, so public passage avoids identifying these as an exactly dated single event.

proposedOverrides.summary: Armenian communities and princes under caliphal rule, with Talin’s dated water inscription.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Separate eighth-century caliphal-era map record; no association with ancient Armenia or armenia-1000.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Exact decoded HB world-700 polygon. Approximate Talin point is inside; Dvin point is outside. Dvin appears only as explicitly regional context.
batchIdentityNotes.evidenceLimits: Dvin finds retain fifth- to eighth-century ranges. Anania is explicitly seventh-century background, not assigned to an eighth-century school. No unsupported hospital, household toilet, universal schooling or medical-treatment claim. Talin script is a checked published transcription, not a fresh decipherment.
